title: Reentrancy in DemoVault.withdraw drains the whole vault
description: DemoVault.withdraw() sends ETH to the caller before zeroing the caller's recorded balance, so a malicious receiver contract can re-enter withdraw() and be paid its full balance again on every re-entry. A 1-ether attacker drains the entire vault, including other users' deposits. (Intentional demo bug in DemoVault.sol.)
root_cause: Checks-interactions-effects ordering: the external call at DemoVault.sol withdraw() precedes the balance update (balances[msg.sender] = 0), so the balance check on re-entry still sees the pre-withdrawal balance.
intended_behavior: Each withdrawal pays the caller exactly its recorded balance once; no caller can withdraw more than it deposited, and no caller can withdraw other users' funds.

trace.description: Public withdraw() reads the caller's balance and checks it is non-zero.
The attacker's receive() callback re-enters withdraw() while the vault still holds funds.
The external call pays the caller before the balance is zeroed, so every re-entry pays again.

evidence.description: External call precedes the state update (call at this line, balance zeroed later).
Balance is zeroed only after the external call returns.
Foundry test testReentrancyDrainsVault: 1-ether attacker drains the vault; PASS.
Foundry test testFixedVaultBlocksReentrancy: the same attack fails against DemoVaultFixed; PASS.

conditions.description: No privilege needed: any address that can deposit 1 ether can run the attack.
The vault must hold other users' deposits for the drain to exceed the attacker's own funds.

execution.attacker_perspective: An ordinary depositor with 1 ether, no special role, no victim cooperation.
payloads: Attacker.attack() after funding the Attacker contract with 1 ether
Attacker.receive() re-enters DemoVault.withdraw() while vault balance >= 1 ether
instructions: Deploy DemoVault; a victim deposits 10 ether.
Deploy Attacker pointing at the vault; fund it with 1 ether.
Call Attacker.attack(): it deposits 1 ether, then withdraws; each payout re-enters withdraw().
Or run the packaged PoC: forge test --match-test testReentrancyDrainsVault.
execution.observed_result: Vault balance 0 ether; attacker balance 11 ether (10 ether of victim funds plus its own 1 ether deposit); 10 reentrant calls. Foundry test testReentrancyDrainsVault PASS. Counterfactual: the same attack against DemoVaultFixed fails and all funds stay in place (testFixedVaultBlocksReentrancy PASS).

remediation.strategy: Follow checks-effects-interactions: zero the caller's balance before the external call (see DemoVaultFixed.sol). Consider a reentrancy guard as defense in depth.

likelihood.reason: Any depositor can run it with no privilege, no victim action, and no timing window.

impact.reason: Total loss of all deposited funds: the attacker takes every other user's deposit.

confidence.reason: Demonstrated end-to-end by a passing Foundry PoC, independently re-run, with a passing counterfactual against the fixed contract.
